summary:
No hidden downscale anywhere. Imagery scale, checked against standard markings, is 1.004 ± 0.004. Ratios measured/standard: tennis service box 0.998, singles 1.010, doubles 0.991, baselines 0.990; basketball key 1.006; volleyball attack lines 0.990; zebra pitch 0.991 ± 0.012. Local TM frame vs geodesic: ratio 1.00000000. Blend: METRIC, scale_length 1.0, 0 of 6509 objects with scale != 1, 0 parented. Every spec has scale 1.0. A 10 m Blender cube becomes 1000 uu in UE: the FBX writes UnitScaleFactor 1 (cm), vertices ±5 m, node scale ×100.
The real skew is in the sports courts. The courts block and all court markings sit too far south in the model, by 1.4 to 2.1 m along the local 'v' axis (≈north). The cause is the 2026-09-28 'flush with the pitch' owner note. Google 2026, Bing 2021 and Esri 2020 all put the courts' south edge 1.2-1.45 m north of the pitch's south edge, and the block is 26.0 m deep (model 25.25). Measured court centres are tennis v 14.41, volleyball 14.47, basketball 14.86; the model has 12.78 for all three. Basketball is 14.34 wide (model 14.50). Volleyball is 8.78 x 17.75 (model 8.70 x 17.65).
OK: pitch size (44.56 ± 0.15 x 25.2 ± 0.15 vs 44.45 x 25.25), gazebos (roof 9.150 across flats, centres within 0.4 m), garden path network (0.24/0.44 m), carriageway 14.78, zebra 4.30 m with 0.4/0.6 stripes, stairs, benches.
Fix: the C classroom door frame is built 0.90 x 2.00 m; the reference frame is 0.99 x 2.05 m.
Open: the frame registration between site and buildings. Site specs were drawn on Google z20, buildings and C on Bing. Google minus Bing ground offset is +1.4 ± 0.3 E, +0.47 ± 0.1 N at sports/courts/hall/alley, about 0 in the garden. So the site may sit about 1.4 m east of C. That depends on Bing being lean-free, so it is marked unsure.

global_checks.check: Local frame (campus_frame.py tmerc) vs WGS84 geodesic distances, 10 point pairs up to 604 m
global_checks.result: ratio 1.00000000 for every pair; grid north = true north (north vector has 0.0 px easting in the tile grid)

Uses the same lon/lat to pixel formula as the tile servers. z20 m/px is 0.10961 E and 0.10921 N, the true ellipsoidal anisotropy of Web Mercator, and it is resampled exactly. No scale error introduced.

global_checks.check: Absolute imagery scale (Google z20) from standard markings
global_checks.result: Measured/standard (centre-to-centre of line, with line widths allowed for): service lines 12.72±0.03/12.75; singles 8.26±0.06/8.18; doubles 10.82±0.03/10.92; baselines 23.43±0.03/23.67; basketball key 4.88±0.02/4.85; volleyball attack lines 5.89±0.04/5.95; zebra pitch 0.991±0.012/1.00 (site). Mean 0.996±0.004, so true = image x 1.004±0.004. No downscale (<0.5%).
Pitch outline widths: Google 44.66 x 25.23, Bing 44.56 x 25.16, Esri 44.37 x 24.93. Bing/Google 0.998 / 0.997, Esri/Google 0.993 / 0.988 (within edge error ±0.15-0.3 m).

global_checks.check: Ground offset between imagery sources (lean-free ground windows; edge profiles + NCC)
global_checks.result: Google-Bing: pitch edges (+1.2, +0.45); NCC pitch (+1.62, +0.48) ncc 0.87; courts (+1.62, +0.45); hall yard (+1.60, +0.63); C plaza (+0.85, +0.37); alley south of the garden (+1.04, +0.61); street lane line dy +0.28; garden about (-0.3, -0.3) (low NCC; path fits agree within 0.1). Google-Esri: (+0.35, -0.31) pitch, (0.0, -0.41) courts. The offset is not uniform, so each zone needs its own registration.

Google is a mosaic with non-uniform lean. The C roof vs the Bing-centred model is (+3.67, +1.10), fit rms 0.19 m, h 15.4 m. The A_N roof in Google is about 4.3 m north of Bing's at only h 9.4 m. The '0.29 E / 0.20 N m/m' figure and the BLD_C anchor note (+7.0 E / +4.0 N at the C roof) are NOT reproduced; at C the lean relative to Bing is ≈(0.15, 0.04) m/m.
6509 objects: 0 with scale != 1, 0 with world scale != 1, 0 parented, 0 negative determinant
All 15 BLD_*.json have scale 1.0 (the builder's scale_spec is therefore an identity); SITE/INT specs have none
C walls in local frame 0..29.400 x 0..21.100 (spec 29.4 x 21.1). Sports objects equal the spec rings to the mm, e.g. Pitch_Plinth u -0.100..44.350, v 0.150..25.400.

global_checks.check: Export chain (export_ue.py: global_scale 1, apply_unit_scale True, FBX_SCALE_NONE, -Y/Z axes; tested on a 10 m cube with the identical call)
global_checks.result: FBX UnitScaleFactor 1.0 (cm), node Lcl Scaling 100, Lcl Translation (300,400,500) cm, vertices ±5. In UE the 10 m object = 1000 uu (1 uu = 1 cm, AGENTS.md rule met). The ×100 lives in the node transform. With 'Import Into Level', check once that actor scale = 1 (baked); FBX_SCALE_ALL would give UnitScaleFactor 100 and node scale 1 if needed. UE MCP is down, so this was not verified in the editor.

open_questions: Is Bing lean-free at C and the sports area? If yes, the Google-drawn sports and passage specs sit about (+1.4 E, +0.47 N) relative to C. One laser measurement settles it: C's NE wall corner (model 203.48, 16.27) to the courts' east fence line (model x ≈ 211.0 at y 42-68).
Courts 'flush with the pitch' (owner, 2026-09-28) vs imagery (1.2-1.45 m north offset in 3 sources): tape the courts' S fence vs the pitch's S fence offset along the walkway.

Not measured (out of scope or not visible from above): D forecourt, campus boundary fences, alley stairs/ramps footprints, tree rows (crowns lean in Google), the gate canopy (under crowns), C plaza planters.

UE import: check once that FBX 'Import Into Level' actors show scale 1.0 (node scale 100 baked into the mesh). If they show 100, switch export_ue.py to apply_scale_options='FBX_SCALE_ALL' (tested: UnitScaleFactor 100, node scale 1). The size is correct either way.
Pitch centre circle radius looks ≈3.4 ± 0.3 vs 3.0 in the model (faint paint); a site tape or drone frame would settle it.
